Do not copy any of its three people or text. Second supplied image (Doho) is the protagonist identity and COSTUME reference: one adult male wandering swordsman, black gat, indigo/navy robe, white crossed collar, muted red sash, blue round ornaments, one sword, no scarf. Preserve recognizable facial identity and adult age while translating him to the SET B drawing style.
SHOT A BEFORE THE ACTION: cool dawn at the FIRST CLOSED SHOP on the outer approach to fictional Motgol market. A plain weathered brown wooden double shutter with four vertical panels, two horizontal cross rails and one simple dark metal ring fills the right third. Its plaster-and-timber facade recedes toward screen right; the stone walking path continues right past it into the market. No written signs or letters.
Doho occupies the left third, shown FULL BODY from the entire uncropped black gat to BOTH boots and their ground shadows, at least 6 percent head and foot margin. He is roughly two ordinary steps from the closed shutter, moving left-to-right; body and face turn three-quarter toward the shutter so his expression will remain visible. Frame the real gap to the door, the paving and the route onward. A natural poised walking start, front foot weighted, trailing heel slightly raised. The empty anatomical LEFT hand hangs at his side, ready later to knock on the door. His anatomical RIGHT hand grips the ONE sword hilt beside his RIGHT shoulder; the blade lies behind the upper back toward his LEFT. Use the reference shoulder-sword configuration, not a weapon-drawing pose. All sword parts inside the image; no spare sword or scabbard that could read as a second blade.
Grounded 40mm-like waist-height camera on the street side, steady three-quarter view; no extreme perspective. Door and Doho share a single ground plane and believable scale. Soft cool ambient dawn, weak warm light from upper screen right, matte skin/cloth/wood/stone, restrained metal highlight only. Background simplified and subordinate. No additional people. No magic, combat, mist covering feet, motion blur, text, borders, logos, collage or decorative inset. The keyframe must make the upcoming APPROACH AND KNOCK physically possible.

A.prompt: A four-second cinematic action shot. Match the start frame's SAME Doho, shop, light and drawn matte style. Doho physically WALKS across the stone ground diagonally toward screen RIGHT to the closed wooden shop door. Two purposeful normal walking steps, real alternating boots lifting and planting, pelvis and shoulders transferring weight, robe reacting to each step. Cover the visible gap rather than walking in place or sliding the backdrop. Begin movement promptly after a very brief opening beat and reach the door within the first 2.5 seconds. Then plant both feet within arm's reach, turn his attention to the shutter and begin raising his empty LEFT hand toward the wood; finish before the knock. RIGHT hand keeps the ONE sword resting behind his shoulders in the original grip; left hand performs the free-arm action. The camera stays on the street side and gently reframes only if necessary to keep both feet and the door contact area visible. Keep the whole gat and blade inside frame. Door stays closed. No talking, no smile yet, no extra people, no text, no cut. Prioritize unmistakable locomotion and arrival over a static portrait.

B.prompt: Four-second cinematic action shot of this EXACT Doho at this EXACT closed shutter. His LEFT fist is poised before contact. Within the first second he extends that forearm and the LEFT knuckles make ONE clear physical knock against the wooden door panel just beyond the jamb, not the metal ring. At the contact instant the knuckles stop against the wood; wrist and elbow absorb the tiny impact. Then he withdraws that hand toward his body and lowers it, and waits facing the STILL CLOSED door. The entire knock-and-withdraw action completes within the first two seconds; leave a clear quiet beat of unanswered waiting afterward. Exactly ONE knock, not a loop or drumming. Keep his RIGHT hand and the one sword in their shoulder grip; no weapon movement or second blade. Eyes stay on the door, lips closed, no smile yet. Natural-speed acting, same matte drawn identity, light, panel rails and ring position. Steady camera with a slight motivated push only; the action of the left hand must be unmistakable. No door opening, no dialogue or text, no cut.

C.prompt: Five-second continuous cinematic shot, the same Doho has just received no answer at this closed shop. Make a COMPLETE readable reaction-and-departure. During seconds 0–0.8 he looks from the closed door toward the next closed shop farther to screen RIGHT. During seconds 0.8–1.6 one eyebrow lifts and one corner of his CLOSED mouth forms a brief wry half-smile, with a tiny knowing head tilt: nobody is here, so he moves on. Then during seconds 1.6–4.6 he turns his torso toward screen RIGHT and ACTUALLY WALKS onward along the paved street IN FRONT OF the building, past the shut door, using three natural grounded steps. Show boots lifting and planting, pelvis shifting, robe and left arm swinging with his gait. Cover at least one body-width of real ground; not walking in place, not backdrop sliding, no slow motion. Finish with forward momentum carrying him toward the right side of frame. Keep the wooden door behind him shut. His RIGHT hand keeps the same ONE sword in the shoulder grip, and his LEFT hand stays empty and swings naturally. Same face, full gat, robe colors, door, matte drawn style and dawn light. Camera stays on the same street side and follows only after he begins walking; keep feet readable. No teeth, speech, extra people, text, combat or cuts.

params.prompt: A four-second film shot, using this exact start image and character. The action is one CRISP KNOCK with a clearly visible RECOIL, then unanswered waiting. Doho's LEFT fist first pulls back from the door by about 20 centimeters, then briskly taps the wooden panel ONCE. Immediately upon touching the wood, the fist BOUNCES BACK toward his chest by about 15 centimeters in a quick elastic recoil. This is a light tap, not a punch or a push. The hand never rests against the wood. After the recoil he lowers his left hand all the way to his side and waits, looking at the closed door with a neutral expression. Complete pullback, one tap, recoil and hand-lowering within the first two seconds; the remaining time is the unanswered look. Natural quick wrist-and-elbow movement, no slow motion. RIGHT hand keeps one sword on the shoulder, no grip change; exact same face, gat, clothes, wooden door rails and single ring. Keep the camera still so the left fist's forward-and-back motion is clear. Door remains completely closed. No second tap, no door opening, no smile, dialogue, teeth, text, extra person or cut.
